rungs.title: Finish him
rungs.idea: The king is the target. If you can checkmate, nothing else matters.
rungs.why: A king only moves one square. If every square it could go to is covered, one check ends the game.

rungs.title: Back door
rungs.idea: A rook or queen on the last rank is checkmate when the king has no escape square.
rungs.why: The king's own pawns are a wall in front of it. From behind, a rook check has no answer unless there is an escape square.

rungs.title: Two-pronged
rungs.idea: A fork attacks two things at once. They can only save one.
rungs.why: One move makes two threats. They get one move to answer, so one target is always lost.

rungs.title: Stuck
rungs.idea: Pins and skewers: when pieces line up, the one in front cannot move or the one behind falls.
rungs.why: A pinned piece cannot move, so it cannot defend anything else. Attack the thing it was guarding.

rungs.title: Surprise!
rungs.idea: Move one piece to unmask another. Double check cannot be blocked.
rungs.why: Moving one piece reveals a second attack. Two threats appear in one move. A double check cannot be blocked at all.

rungs.title: Castle, then charge
rungs.idea: Castle early so your king is safe and your rook joins the hunt. f7 is the weak spot.
rungs.why: Castling tucks your king away and brings a rook to the centre in one move. Now you can attack without fear. f7 is weak because only the king defends it.

rungs.title: Bring everyone
rungs.idea: Count attackers against defenders around the king. More attackers wins.
rungs.why: Around the king, count your attackers and their defenders. If you have more, something breaks. Every extra piece you bring makes it certain.

rungs.title: Open the door
rungs.idea: Give up a pawn or a piece to rip open the shelter in front of the king.
rungs.why: The pawns in front of the king are its roof. Give a pawn or a piece to remove them and every line to the king opens at once.

rungs.title: Smother & trap
rungs.idea: Some mates use the king's own pieces as the walls of its prison.
rungs.why: A king surrounded by its own pieces has no escape squares at all. One check from a knight or a rook is mate.

rungs.title: Deflect & decoy
rungs.idea: Pull the defender away, or drag the king onto a bad square.
rungs.why: If one piece guards two things, it can only do one job. Give it a second job and the first one fails.

rungs.title: Ignore the threat
rungs.idea: When attacked, look for a check or a bigger threat first. Then recapture.
rungs.why: A check or a mate threat must be answered first. Make yours before you deal with theirs, and you keep the tempo.

rungs.title: Finishing school
rungs.idea: Longer mates and pawn promotions. King and queen, king and rook: close the game.
rungs.why: A pawn that reaches the end becomes a queen. With king and queen, or king and rook, drive the enemy king to the edge where it cannot run.
